title: Orchestrated probing and fallback policies for reranker clusters to improve availability and tail latency
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We are seeing intermittent increases in 95th/99th percentile latency for the reranking endpoint during regional capacity pressure and noisy neighbors. Current fallback behaviour is ad hoc and tied to capacity signals; it lacks a proactive mechanism to detect degraded clusters and automated, policy-driven choices between fallbacks (smaller model, cached results, local index, or degraded scoring).

Goal: Introduce an orchestration layer that (1) proactively probes reranker clusters to estimate healthy request throughput/latency, (2) surfaces a per-cluster health score computed from probes + recent request telemetry, and (3) uses a policy engine to pick fallbacks per request with gradual rollouts. This should reduce client-observed tail latency and error rate with minimal impact on quality and cost.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Probe scheduler runs in each region and publishes a 10s-updated 'health_score' per reranker pool to the control plane.
2) Requests routed to degraded pools are automatically diverted according to policy: prefer cached prefix responses, then smaller rerank model, then local approximate rerank, with thresholds configurable per-customer.
3) End-to-end SLO improvement: reduce rerank 99th latency by at least 25% during simulated capacity pressure while keeping mean NDCG@10 drop < 2%.
4) Feature gated and can be toggled per-customer; rollout plan documented and can be rolled back via console.
5) Integration tests and canary deployed to prod-priv before full rollout.
comments: 2025-01-12 — Initial design sketch posted to Confluence; highlighted trade-offs between probe frequency and probe-induced noise. (Leila Chen)

2025-01-20 — Spike results: probe using lightweight synthetic queries added ~0.6% overhead; health score correlates with 95th latency (r=0.78). PoC code in branch rerank/health-probe-poC. (Marco Ruiz)

2025-01-27 — Design review with Platform and SRE. Decision: use passive telemetry + adaptive probing; probes back off when region close to capacity. Add circuit-breaker state machine with OPEN/HALF_OPEN/CLOSED and exponential backoff. Action: implement circuit-breaker transitions in control plane. (Design approved)
2025-01-31 — PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/reranker/pull/4274 implementing probe scheduler and health score API. Needs load test and security review. (PR author: Marco Ruiz)

2025-02-03 — Load testing in staging with fault injection showed a 32% reduction in 99th latency when fallback policy enabled; small drop in NDCG observed for a subset of queries (1.4% average). Metrics dashboard: grafana.redwood.ai/d/rerank/health-probe-experiment. (SRE: Daniel Park)
2025-02-04 — Security note: probes need service identity + rate limits. Submitted for security review (sec-2025-089). (Marco Ruiz)
notes: Trade-offs considered: aggressive fallbacks reduce latency but can harm quality; default policy will prefer cached/local approximations for latency-sensitive customers and will keep heavier accurate reranks for enterprise customers that opted into higher-latency SLOs. We also considered hedged requests but excluded them initially due to cost amplification during multi-region storms.
